arxiv-2102-04903.description: Abstract . Accurate user interest modeling is important for news recommendation. Most existing methods for news recommendation rely on implicit feedbacks like click for inferring user interests and model training. However, click behaviors usually contain heavy noise, and cannot help infer complicated user interest such as dislike.

arxiv-2106-11611.title: Tetrahedron instantons Preprint: DESY 21-087
arxiv-2106-11611.creator: Elli Pomoni, Wenbin Yan, Xinyu Zhang
arxiv-2106-11611.description: Abstract We introduce and study tetrahedron instantons, which can be realized in string theory by D 1 1 -branes probing a configuration of intersecting D 7 7 -branes in flat spacetime with a proper constant B B -field. Physically they capture instantons on ℂ 3 \mathbb{C}^{3} in the presence of the most general intersecting real codimension-two supersymmetric defects.

arxiv-2108-09313.title: Weyl hydrodynamics in a strong magnetic field
arxiv-2108-09313.creator: Siyu Zhu, Grigory Bednik, Sergey Syzranov
arxiv-2108-09313.description: Abstract We study the hydrodynamic transport of electrons in a Weyl semimetal in a strong magnetic field. Impurity scattering in a Weyl semimetal with two Weyl nodes is strongly anisotropic as a function of the direction of the field and is significantly suppressed if the field is perpendicular to the separation between the nodes in momentum space.

arxiv-2510-04160.title: CLEAR: A Closed-Form Minimal-Sensor TDOA/FDOA Estimator for Moving-Source IoT Localization
arxiv-2510-04160.creator: Mohammad Kazzazi, Mohammad Morsali, and Rouhollah Amiri
arxiv-2510-04160.description: Abstract This paper presents CLEAR—a Closed-form Localization Estimator with A Reduced sensor network. The proposed method is a computationally efficient, two-stage estimator that fuses Time-Difference-of-Arrival (TDOA) and Frequency-Difference-of-Arrival (FDOA) measurements with a minimal number of sensors. CLEAR localizes a moving source in N N -dimensional space using only N + 1 N{+}1 sensors, achieving the theoretical minimum sensor count.

arxiv-2601-00903.title: A Taxonomy of Magnetostatic Field Lines
arxiv-2601-00903.creator: Joel Franklin, David Griffiths, Darrell Schroeter
arxiv-2601-00903.description: Abstract Contrary to widespread belief, magnetostatic field lines do not ordinarily form closed loops. Why, then, are they in fact closed for so many familiar examples? What other topologies are possible, and what current configurations generate them?
